Article Title: Military-civil integration key to robust def ecosystem to tackle challenges: Rajnath
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh addresses the AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations at DRDO Bhawan in New Delhi on Monday

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security and technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability and the effective application of rules and regulations.Addressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in Delhi on Aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.Rajnath underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas — policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences.“Military officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory.When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,” Rajnath said.Explaining with the example of ‘cyber warfare’, the minister stated that if officers of the AFHQ civilian services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the defence forces. He said a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, AFHQ civilian services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.Rajnath called upon the AFHQ civilian services to evolve into the “strategic brain” of India’s defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.While he acknowledged the AFHQ civilian services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.“A military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must focus on strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,” Rajnath said.
Article Summary: Defence minister rajnath singh underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry. Addressing the 85th armed forces headquarters (afhq) civilian services day celebrations in delhi on aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of 'nation first'

Article Title: SKM announces farmers' protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, from November 26
Article Text:
November 26 also marks the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmers’ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of the students’ protests here at Jantar Mantar, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM)—the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago—on Monday announced that it would restart protests at 100 locations, including Delhi, across India from November 26 - the day which will mark the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmers’ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in December 2021.The protests will demand a law guaranteeing minimum support price (MSP), repeal of all free trade agreements and no India-US FTA, and a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness.The SKM’s demand list also includes four other demands such as scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs. 31,000 payable to all workers as well as restoration of the previous rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, the Seed Bill 2025, and the NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition.“The protest will not be called off until all seven principal demands are achieved,” said P Krishnaprasad of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), a constituent of SKM.“The decisive mass struggle, coordinated with joint platforms and organisations of workers, farmers, agricultural workers, students, youth, women and all other social sections facing the brunt of corporate attack under the NDA regime will advance based on worker-peasant unity to end the prolonged agrarian crisis and labour exploitation, and to build a modern democratic, federal, secular India,” he said while announcing the overall protest plan of the SKM.
Article Summary: November 26 marks the sixth anniversary of the year-long farmers’ protest, which culminated in the repeal of the three farm laws in december 2021. The protests will demand a law guaranteeing minimum support price (msp), repeal of all free trade agreements and no india-us fta, and a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness.

NEW DELHI: Parliamentary standing committee on communications and information technology chairman Nishikant Dubey on Monday said Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise over the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video, warning that the social media giant could lose its safe harbour protection if it failed to do so.Dubey's remarks came after Meta apologised before the parliamentary panel, saying the PM Modi's video was removed due to an error. However, members of the committee said the issue went beyond an apology and demanded accountability for the incident.Addressing reporters after chairing the committee meeting, Dubey said, "...Understand the situation that has arisen within the algorithm. What Meta India did, what X did, and what YouTube did is a matter that the country should know. If you look at the viewership algorithm of the BJP, Congress, Samajwadi Party, and Aam Aadmi Party, the viewership is only 23 million. And those who are neither registered parties nor registered NGOs, their algorithm is 27 million. All political parties together are at 23-24 million. An anti-reservation forum has just been formed five or six days ago, and it reached 7 million. The reason for that is that they have a policy of giving preference to newcomers."On the removal of the Prime Minister's video, he said, "The second question is that Meta India removed the Prime Minister's content. This is not the first time Meta India has done this. If you recall, Zuckerberg himself made a statement in January regarding the 2024 elections and later apologized. This shows that his intention is to destabilise the country. When a video of the Prime Minister of India can be removed, and they themselves admitted that the content was missing for five hours, from 12:30 am to 5:00 am, this is a very serious matter. Our committee has said two things and has clearly stated that the apology should come from Zuckerberg. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him."Dubey also raised concerns over the handling of child sexual abuse material and other objectionable content on social media platforms.He said, "CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) is another issue. YouTube also has that content. Meta also has that content, and they do not remove content related to child abuse. They do not remove content related to women. Both these rules of the Government of India are very strict, and on top of that, they do not listen to the Home Ministry. They do not listen to the IT Ministry either. So, we have said that in all these matters, and in many other matters, you know that the Chief Minister of the Congress government of Telangana has filed an FIR against Meta India. We have said that safe harbour should be removed in all these matters..."Earlier in the day, Meta apologised before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, saying the removal of PM Modi's Facebook video was the result of an error. According to ANI sources, several committee members questioned Meta officials and said the issue was not about an apology but about fixing accountability. Members also sought details on the company's action against controversial and objectionable content on its platforms.ANI sources said, "The Parliamentary Standing Committee on IT took a tough stance over the removal of PM Modi’s video from Facebook. During the committee meeting, several members posed tough questions to Meta officials. Meta officials apologized, stating that the PM’s video was removed due to an error. Several committee members said the issue was not about an apology, but about fixing accountability. Committee members also demanded legal action against the Meta official responsible for removing the video. Members further sought details from Meta on what action the company has taken regarding controversial and objectionable content present on its platforms. Meeting is still underway."The meeting, attended by representatives of Meta, Google , YouTube, X and Snapchat, along with officials from the Union home ministry and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), was convened to discuss the regulation of social and digital media platforms.The controversy stems from the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Modi's Facebook post in which he addressed India's youth and promised stringent action against paper leaks. While Meta restored the content and attributed the removal to a technical error, the MeitY termed the explanation "inadequate", saying the issue also concerned national security and public order.Separately, Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police has registered cases against Meta India head Arun Srinivas and certain Facebook and Instagram accounts over allegedly morphed and AI-generated posts targeting the Prime Minister.
Article Summary: Meta apologises before parliament panel over removal of pm modi's facebook video. Members of the committee said the issue went beyond an apology and demanded accountability for the incident. Members also demanded legal action against the meta official responsible for removing the video.

Article Title: Lok Sabha clears bill to increase number of Supreme Court judges, without debate
Article Text:
The bill proposes to increase the number of Supreme Court judges from the present 33 to 37, excluding the CJI

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Monday passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges from the present 33 to 37 (excluding the Chief Justice of India).The bill, which will now be sent to the Rajya Sabha for consideration, was passed without a debate as opposition members continued raising slogans over the NEET paper leak and the alleged theft of donations from the Ram temple.After a brief introductory statement by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, the Chair invited MPs to speak. However, with the sloganeering continuing, the bill was put to a voice vote and passed.Following the passage of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, the House was adjourned for the day.On May 5, the Union Cabinet approved the introduction of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 in Parliament. The legislation seeks to amend the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, which provides for an increase in the number of Supreme Court judges, excluding the Chief Justice.The government has argued that increasing the number of judges would enable the Supreme Court to function more efficiently and effectively, while ensuring the speedy delivery of justice.The sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court was last increased from 30 to 33 judges, excluding the Chief Justice of India, through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, which amended the original Act.
Article Summary: The bill proposes to increase the number of supreme court judges from the present 33 to 37, excluding the cji. Opposition members continued raising slogans over the neet paper leak and the alleged theft of donations from the ram temple. The bill will now be sent to the rajya sabha for consideration.

Article Title: 'Do not befriend Kaafirs': Pakistani general levels terror allegations against India
Article Text:
Pakistan's military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry

Pakistan's military spokesperson, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, has sparked controversy after saying in a video that Muslims should not befriend "kaafirs" (non-believers), warning that those who do would no longer be considered among the faithful."Do not befriend kaafirs (non-believers) and leave the faithful. If you do that, there's a problem. Then you are not among the Muslims," Chaudhry said while addressing a press conference.“Now our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,” he added.The remarks were made during a wider media briefing that focused on Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations, the security situation in Balochistan, and the country's ties with Afghanistan.Taking a jibe at India-Afghanistan ties, Chaudhry claimed that the Afghan Taliban regime's "business" was terrorism, alleging that it used militancy to sustain its economy, state institutions and diplomacy.“Even their diplomacy is centred on terrorism. What is common between India and Afghanistan, except their DNA? The only thing common is terrorism,” Chaudhary said, as cited by Dawn.Chaudhry also claimed that around 300 Indian websites were being used to support terrorism-related activities in Balochistan, while more than 1,000 social media accounts and what he described as a "hostile diaspora" were involved in spreading propaganda linked to terrorism.“First, an event or incident is seeded, right or wrong, and then it is framed by initiators, who hand it over to amplifiers. Then mass amplification is done by mainstream Indian media, channels and their print media as well, from where it is picked up by international media, and then you take it and run it as facts," he said.The DG ISPR said the government was also working to strengthen the police force, including by deploying newly recruited assistant superintendents of police (ASPs) to Balochistan and providing bulletproof vehicles, among other measures.The remarks come amid a series of attacks on Pakistani security forces across Balochistan last month, with armed clashes also reported during military operations in the Mastung and Kech districts, according to The Balochistan Post (TBP).The insurgency in Balochistan has been led by several separatist groups, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), which has waged a long-running campaign against Pakistan's federal government. The group has frequently targeted security personnel and infrastructure in the province and has also carried out attacks in other parts of the country, including Karachi.According to Pakistan's 2023 census, Balochistan is home to around 15 million people and is rich in natural resources, including coal, gold, copper and natural gas. The BLA maintains that these resources should belong to the people of Balochistan and opposes the federal government's control over their extraction and the province's security.
Article Summary: Lieutenant general ahmed sharif chaudhry said muslims should not befriend "kaafirs" (non-believers) he warned that those who do would no longer be considered among the faithful. The remarks were made during a wider media briefing that focused on pakistan's counter-terrorism operations.

Article Title: Nolan Wells case update: Mississippi officials issue urgent warning after fake toxicology report spreads across social media
Article Text:
Fake Nolan Wells toxicology report prompts warning from Mississippi officials

Nolan Wells investigation remains active as officials urge public to rely on verified information

Mississippi officials are pushing back against a wave of online misinformation after a fake toxicology report tied to the death of Nolan Wells began circulating on social media. Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell issued a public warning, stressing that the document is fraudulent and urging people to rely only on verified updates as investigators continue working on the high-profile case.The warning came after a document claiming to be Nolan Wells' toxicology report gained traction across multiple social media platforms. According to state officials, the report is entirely fabricated and has no connection to the ongoing investigation.In a statement shared online, Mississippi Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell made it clear that the circulating document should not be treated as legitimate."The purported toxicology report from Nolan Wells circulating through social media on various outlets is fraudulent," Tindell wrote. "Nolan's family, friends, and most importantly, Nolan himself, deserve better."His remarks reflect growing concern over how quickly false information can spread during active criminal investigations.In recent years, fabricated documents, edited images and AI-generated content have increasingly appeared online, making it more difficult for the public to separate verified facts from misinformation.The commissioner urged social media users to think carefully before sharing content that has not been confirmed by authorities, particularly in sensitive cases involving grieving families.Tindell also addressed the broader issue of misinformation fueled by advancing technology. While discussing the fake report, he warned that artificial intelligence and social media have created an environment where false claims can spread rapidly."Fraudsters, AI, and social media are a recipe for disaster. All they want you to do is click and share, don't!" he said.His message serves as a reminder that viral posts are not necessarily accurate, especially when they claim to reveal confidential investigative records.At this stage, officials have not released an official toxicology report related to Nolan Wells' death. Any documents claiming otherwise should be treated with skepticism unless they come directly from law enforcement or other authorized agencies.Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding Wells' death, and no official findings regarding toxicology have been announced. Investigators have repeatedly emphasized that information released through official channels remains the only reliable source for updates.The spread of fabricated material can complicate ongoing investigations by creating confusion, encouraging speculation and placing additional emotional strain on those closest to the case. It can also undermine public confidence in legitimate reporting when false claims circulate unchecked.As interest in the Wells investigation continues, state officials are asking the public to slow down before sharing sensational posts and instead wait for confirmed information. For investigators, preserving the integrity of the case remains the priority. For Wells' family and friends, officials say accuracy and respect matter just as much.Until authorities formally release new evidence or investigative findings, the alleged toxicology report circulating online should not be considered credible. Mississippi officials remain focused on the investigation while encouraging the public to help stop the spread of misinformation rather than contribute to it.
Article Summary: Fake nolan wells toxicology report prompts warning from mississippi officials. Public safety commissioner sean tindell issued a public warning. He urged people to rely on verified updates as investigators continue working on the high-profile case. No official findings regarding toxicology have been announced.

Article Title: 'Accept mandate with bowed head': BJP after setback in Bankipur bypoll, promises review

The BJP has full faith in democracy and constitutional arrangements and believes in correcting its shortcomings through introspection and review,” Saraogi said.

Filing an extension before visa expiry may not save you from ICE arrest.

What is the case of Chantal Morales Rojas?

Amid a sudden spike in arrests at domestic airports, immigration lawyer Poonam Gupta said what is happening is not a fault of the visa holders; it is assumptions going wrong. Citing the recent case of Oakland's Chantal Morales Rojas who was arrested on the accusation of visa overstay, Gupta said Rojas came to the US legally on a J-1 visa as an au pair. Before it expired, she timely filed an extension application, but that did not stop ICE officials from detaining her. And she was released only after a court order.Gupta urged visa holders not to assume that they won't be detained just because they filed an extension for their visa on time and becaue they do not have any criminal record."A timely-filed extension or status application legally starts a period of authorized stay. ICE is arresting people anyway. At airport check-in counters and gates, including travelers with pending green card, asylum, and extension applications, at least 27 arrests across 15 airports in 9 states in recent weeks, per an internal DHS memo obtained by ABC News," Gupta wrote in a LinkedIn post."Two things people assume protect them. Right now, neither reliably does: A pending extension application: legally, this starts authorized stay; A domestic flight: no border, no customs, should be lower risk," she explained."This isn't a loophole or a technicality — it's the law working as intended, and ICE treating it as if it doesn't," she said urging visa holders to consult their immigration attorneys before booking domestic flights.Chantal Morales Rojas, an Oakland resident originally from Ecuador, took part in a short group trip to Denver for a frisbee tournament but she was stopped, questioned and then arrested on the jetway of her flight home on July 20. The administration said she was detained as she overstayed her visa that expired on January 4, 2025. She was taken to the GEO Detention Facility in Aurora, Colorado, while her friends started raising money for legal help.Last week, Rojas was released on a $3,000 bond.Rojas filed an extension of her visa before it expired but it remained pending at the time of her arrest.
Article Summary: Filing an extension before visa expiry may not save you from ice arrest. Immigration lawyer poonam gupta said what is happening is not a fault of the visa holders. At least 27 arrests across 15 airports in 9 states in recent weeks, according to internal dhs memo.

Jairam Ramesh accuses PM Modi of playing 'victim card'

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth.He said the Prime Minister should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card." He further alleged that the Prime Minister "uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents" and "very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself.""He uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents. He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." He alleged that the remark was "an insult to the nation and to our youth", adding that young people had suffered under the government's policies and were instead seeking an apology from the Prime Minister."The Prime Minister’s InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one," Ramesh added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a video late at night that carried a message against abusive language and hate, saying "abuses never solve anything," amid a controversy over alleged derogatory remarks made against him by a woman from Noida during a protest in Delhi."Abuses never solve anything. Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.

Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:
Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security

'First selection' after Modi became PM

Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit shah presented lokmanya tilak award to ajit doval and hailed his role in india's national security. Shah said the nsa's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening india's security architecture and defence preparedness.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The us state department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The policy is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including bangladesh, nepal and bhutan. India is not on the list of countries covered by the programme.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from London

: Economic fugitive Vijay Mallya invited fellow billionaire Nirav Modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking Regent's Park where the pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London before his arrest, the final podcast of the "Diamond King", released Friday, claims.A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact... "Mallya told him he was a fool for living so openly and told him he was too exposed, but Nirav didn't listen.""It's possible Mallya's blueprint gave Nirav the confidence he didn't need to hide." But Nirav did not get bail and has been in a London jail for seven years.Despite an Interpol red notice, Nirav "would regularly stop for a cup of coffee at a cafe in Oxford Street where he would sit reading newspapers... where anyone could see him," the source said. However, he started taking precautions later. To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."
Article Summary: Vijay mallya invited nirav modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking regent's park. The pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in london. A source in the diamond trade who tipped off telegraph about nirav's location, leading to his arrest, claims in episode 4: "mallya and nirav were in contact"

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its north african enclave of ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across europe.

Article Title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake hits Italy; buildings damaged, four injured
Article Text:
4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four (Reuters image)

A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck the volcanic Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields) area near the southern Italian city of Naples on Friday, injuring four people, damaging buildings and churches. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.The earthquake struck at 7.46 pm (local time), with its epicentre in the Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km (2 miles), according to Italy's National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.The Italian fire service said minor damage was reported to buildings in and around Naples, but added that emergency crews had not received any immediate requests for rescue or assistance, as cited by Reuters.As a precaution, local authorities suspended rail and metro services while inspections were carried out.Italian media described the tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded in the Campi Flegrei area, prompting residents in several neighbourhoods to rush onto the streets as the ground shook.Campi Flegrei, a densely populated volcanic caldera that spans much of western Naples, has witnessed increasingly frequent seismic activity in recent years, prompting Italian authorities to intensify monitoring of the area.While low-intensity tremors are common in the region, stronger earthquakes have revived concerns over a repeat of the seismic crisis of the early 1980s, which caused widespread disruption and forced thousands of residents to evacuate their homes.Italy is prone to earthquakes due to its geological setting. In 2016, a series of powerful quakes struck central Italy, devastating parts of the Lazio, Umbria and Marche regions and killing around 300 people.The country's deadliest earthquake in recent decades was the 6.9-magnitude Irpinia quake in southern Italy in November 1980, which claimed about 2,700 lives and devastated hundreds of towns.
Article Summary: 4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes italy, injures four people. It struck the volcanic campi flegrei (phlegraean fields) area near the southern italian city of naples. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.

Article Title: US Marine F-35 fighter jet crashes in San Diego, pilot ejects safely
Article Text:
Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

A US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday, with the pilot ejecting safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire, military officials said.The fighter aircraft, attached to the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing and Marine Aircraft Group 11, went down at around 10 am local time near the air station. The Marine Corps described the incident as an "aircraft mishap".First Lieutenant Blake Starbuck told Fox News that the crash was a "Class A mishap involving a Marine Corps F-35B in the vicinity of MCAS Miramar".Lieutenant Starbuck confirmed that the pilot successfully ejected and was safely recovered after the aircraft came down. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.Starbuck said he could not immediately confirm the purpose of the flight, including whether the aircraft had been taking off, landing or carrying out a training mission.He also said there was no immediate information about any injuries or fatalities linked to the crash.Television footage from SkyRanger 7 showed the wreckage split into two large sections in the middle of a burnt field roughly the size of a football pitch.Large flames and thick black smoke rose from the crash site, which was located north of State Route 52, making the fire visible to motorists on the nearby highway. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department said it had joined efforts to contain the brush fire triggered by the crash.However, officials said the military remains in charge of the crash site and will lead the investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: Us marine corps f-35 fighter jet crashed near marine corps air station (mcas) miramar in san diego. Pilot ejected safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.
